about: Facts behind the study cards of the Binwise list of 28 November 2026 (card chunks c1 to c5): each bottle as the catalogue research/winelist-2026-11-28.json prints it (its ledger key, entry n, bin, vintage, size, the printed price with its dollar sign and the paste line), and each fact a card states that the guide and the paste do not, with how it is known. A fact found by search names where, and every fact rests on two sources or one primary source (the producer, its importer, the appellation body); a fact that could not be confirmed is recorded as left out. Nothing here is a score or a price the list does not print. Under mentions, the other bottles of the list the cards name as a step or a mix-up, each as the catalogue holds it.

bottles.name: Lemelson "Thea's Selection" Willamette Valley
bottles.card: Lemelson ‘Thea’s Selection’ Willamette Valley Pinot Noir 2022

facts.fact: Thea’s Selection is Lemelson Vineyards’ house Pinot Noir, a blend of fruit from its organically farmed estate vineyards, which span three sub-regions (AVAs) of the Willamette Valley; listings give five or seven estate vineyards by vintage, so the card gives no count.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: the winery’s note as reproduced on wine.com (Thea’s Selection 2022 and 2021); the importer’s (Winebow) Lemelson sheet; a retailer note (wineaccess.com) that most of the fruit is from the Yamhill-Carlton District, which the card leaves out as one source

facts.fact: Lemelson Vineyards is an estate winery at Carlton, in the Willamette Valley, farmed organically from the start.
facts.how: already in the house (component wine-story-lemelson, from the glass sheet research of 15 November 2026); the organic farming confirmed again by the winery’s note on wine.com and the Winebow sheet

facts.fact: The 2022 tastes of red currant, tart cranberry and fresh mint (the winery’s note), tart cherry and cranberry (a critic’s note quoted by a retailer); medium bodied with chalky tannins and snappy freshness (the winery’s note); medium bodied (Decanter’s listing). Checked 28 November 2026: no source calls it silky, so the card says fine, chalky tannin and bright, not silky or low in tannin.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: wine.com winemaker notes for the 2022; a retailer’s quotation of a Wine Spectator note; decanter.com wine review listing. No score is carried.

facts.fact: 2022 in the Willamette Valley: a cold, wet spring and an April frost, then a long, warm fall and a late harvest.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: the Oregon Wine Board’s 2022 Oregon harvest report (industry.oregonwine.org) and Decanter’s 2022 Willamette Valley vintage report

facts.fact: The winery’s cellar practice for this cuvée in 2022 (yeast, oak, fining) was not confirmed: the Winebow sheet gives native yeast and no fining or filtering for another vintage. Left out; the card sends it to the sommelier.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026; no 2022 technical sheet found

facts.fact: Who Thea is was not confirmed by any source read, and whether that person is living is unknown; the card names no one and sends the question to the sommelier.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026

facts.fact: Domaine Daulny is at Verdigny, in the Sancerre hills, and farms about fifteen hectares in some fifty separate plots.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: the importer’s page (charlesnealselections.com, Domaine Etienne Daulny) and Flatiron Wines’ importer notes; one other listing says sixteen hectares, so the card says about fifteen

facts.fact: The Sancerre blends plots on varied soils, clay with flint (silex) and Portlandian and Kimmeridgian limestone, and is fermented in stainless steel.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: charlesnealselections.com (most of the wine fermented and aged in stainless steel, a small share in large old barrels) and Flatiron Wines (stainless steel only). The two differ on oak, so the card says fermented in stainless steel and sends any oak to the sommelier.

facts.fact: The 2024 tastes of lime, green apple and white blossom with a chalky finish.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: retailer notes on the 2024 (winebazaar.com, missionliquor.com, and Flatiron’s note on the Réserve 2024 for the chalky finish)

facts.fact: 2024 in Sancerre: record rain, downy mildew and low yields; light wines with very crisp acidity.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: the Centre-Loire wine body’s 2024 harvest report (vins-centre-loire.com) and Decanter’s Centre-Loire 2024 report

facts.fact: On the list of 28 November 2026 the only white Sancerre under $100 is this bottle: the others are Pascal Cotat La Grande Côte 2023 ($255), Les Monts Damnés 2022 ($350) and the Vatan Clos la Néore magnum ($920); the Sautereau Sancerre 2022 at $80 is printed under Loire red.
facts.how: research/winelist-2026-11-28.json entries 653 to 655 and 1459

facts.fact: Pouilly-Fumé is the Sauvignon Blanc appellation across the Loire from Sancerre.
facts.how: knowledge, certain

facts.fact: The person who runs the domaine is not named: whether living is not known to the card, and the rule names no living person.
facts.how: house rule

bottles.name: Domaine Maurice Charleux "La Fussière" Maranges Burgundy FR

facts.fact: La Fussière is a Premier Cru climat of Maranges; Charleux’s 2022 is sold as Maranges 1er Cru La Fussière, so the label reads Maranges Premier Cru though the list prints only Maranges.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: decanter.com wine review (Domaine Maurice Charleux & Fils, Maranges, 1er Cru La Fussière 2022) and winelibrary.com (2022 Maranges 1er Cru La Fussière); the Burgundy pages of the list print La Fussière under Maranges Premier Cru for Matrot and Morey (entries 2124, 2125)

facts.fact: Domaine Maurice Charleux et Fils is at Dezize-lès-Maranges, about four kilometers southwest of Santenay; it was founded in 1894 by Ferdinand Charleux, who owned a little over half a hectare, and farms just under ten hectares of Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: the importer’s page (charlesnealselections.com, Domaine Maurice Charleux et Fils), the primary source; the Hachette guide’s producer page names the domaine at Dezize. Ferdinand Charleux, the founder of 1894, is named as a person long dead.

facts.fact: The domaine ferments its reds with indigenous yeasts and bottles with a light filtration about a year after the wine goes into barrel.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: charlesnealselections.com (the importer, primary), the domaine’s general practice; no technical sheet for the 2022 red was found, so new oak share and stems are left out

facts.fact: La Fussière is the largest climat of Maranges; its soil is limestone over marl; the Premier Cru vineyards of Maranges face south below the Montagne des Trois Croix, and there are seven. Checked 28 November 2026: the Boisset La Fussière sheet gives a south and southeast exposure, so the card says facing south and southeast; Maranges lies wholly in the Saône-et-Loire, so the card no longer says the Côte d’Or runs into it.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: charlesnealselections.com (largest climat); the Boisset (Bouchard Aîné) La Fussière sheet and a retailer’s note (limestone and marl); Decanter’s Maranges feature and the Burgundy Report village profile (south facing, seven Premiers Crus). The domaine’s holding is 1.82 hectares by the importer and 30 ares by Hachette, so the card gives none.

facts.fact: Maranges is the southernmost appellation of the Côte de Beaune, just inside the Saône-et-Loire, shared by three villages: Cheilly-lès-Maranges, Dezize-lès-Maranges and Sampigny-lès-Maranges; almost all its wine is red Pinot Noir.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: the INAO’s Maranges sheet (inao.gouv.fr), Decanter’s Maranges feature and the Burgundy Report

facts.fact: The 2022 tastes of ripe cherry and raspberry with an earthy, mushroom edge; firm tannins and fine acidity; medium bodied.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: winelibrary.com and firstleaf.com notes on the Charleux 2022 (cherry, raspberry, mushroom, medium body); the Hachette guide (a solid tannic frame and a fine acidity that carries the finish); Decanter’s listing (medium bodied, oaked). Checked 28 November 2026: the fruit and mushroom words rest on one retailer (winelibrary.com; the firstleaf page carries no tasting note), and dense was not found, so the card says fine acidity in its place

facts.fact: 2022 in Burgundy: hot and dry, a generous crop after the frost of 2021, reds ripe with fresh, red fruit.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: Decanter’s Burgundy 2022 reports and The World of Fine Wine, both reporting the BIVB’s figures

facts.fact: On the list of 28 November 2026 two other growers’ La Fussière print under Maranges Premier Cru: Thierry & Pascale Matrot 2015 (bin 224210, $78) and Vincent & Sophie Morey 2022 (bin 23113, $105).
facts.how: research/winelist-2026-11-28.json entries 2124 and 2125

facts.fact: The list prints two vintages at one price: the 2017 (b2280, n 2280, bin 22522, line 11809) and the 2021 (b2281, n 2281, bin 26724, line 11814), both $155. The card is the 2017, the one to open tonight; the 2021 is named in its service note and kept notes.
facts.how: the catalogue research/winelist-2026-11-28.json and the paste, lines 11809 to 11818

facts.fact: Bin 22522 is also printed for the Domaine Tempier Bandol 2023 (n 1161, line 6006, $120, France ~ Other ~ White > Provence).
facts.how: the catalogue research/winelist-2026-11-28.json n 1161 and the paste line 6006

facts.fact: Château Gloria was put together from 1942 by Henri Martin out of parcels bought from Saint-Julien classed growths, and stands outside the 1855 classification; Château Saint-Pierre is a sister estate of the same family.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: the estate's own site (chateau-gloria.com, A creation story: the name registered in 1942, the largest non classified estate of Saint-Julien); Wikipedia (Château Gloria; Henri Martin); The Wine Doctor; Domaines Henri Martin. The first purchase is given variously (four or six hectares, from Duhart-Milon or Beychevelle), so the card names no first seller and no first area. Henri Martin died in 1991 (Wikipedia, Henri Martin (winemaker)); the producer record in research/winelist/producers-d.json names him too

facts.fact: The 2017 blend is 61 percent Cabernet Sauvignon, 26 percent Merlot, 8 percent Petit Verdot and 5 percent Cabernet Franc, aged 14 months in French oak, 40 percent new. Checked 28 November 2026 by the fact checker of chunk c4: the blend confirmed by wine.com and Uncorked; 14 months and 40 percent new by Mr Wheeler and Delectable.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: wine.com, Millesima and Farr Vintners for the blend; three retailer and cellar listings for 14 months and 40 percent new (one retailer's 50 percent new is the estate's general figure). No château sheet for 2017 was found, so the card sends the château's own sheet to the sommelier

facts.fact: The 2017 tastes of cassis and plum, cedar and a touch of violet, medium bodied and fresh, with supple tannin. Checked 28 November 2026 by the fact checker of chunk c4: cassis leaf rests on one critic’s note (Julia Harding’s, quoted by Uncorked), so the card no longer says it; cassis and violet are in the Decanter note quoted by Sokolin and the wine.com note, plum, cedar and medium body in the Mr Wheeler note and the wine.com listing (medium bodied, melting tannins).
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: Decanter's review (lifted cassis and cassis leaf, very fresh); the wine.com note (cassis, violets); the Guide Hachette 2021 (cassis and spice, supple, integrated tannin); a retailer note (blackcurrant, plum, cedar, medium bodied, soft). No score is carried

facts.fact: 2017: the late April frost cut the crop across much of Bordeaux, but the vineyards of Saint-Estèphe, Pauillac and Saint-Julien nearest the Gironde were largely spared. Checked 28 November 2026 by the fact checker of chunk c4: Jancis Robinson’s frost reports give Saint-Julien only a little damage, inland towards Saint-Laurent, and name Lagrange as a Saint-Julien estate the frost did hit; Gloria’s parcels lie across the commune, so the card says Saint-Julien largely escaped the frost and claims nothing for the estate’s own vines.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: Jancis Robinson (Bordeaux 2017, where the frost hit; the estuary's effect on the three northern Médoc appellations); a press report of the frost (the communes closest to the river largely untouched)

facts.fact: 2021 in Bordeaux was a cool vintage of lighter, lower alcohol reds; the 2021 Gloria is 61 percent Cabernet Sauvignon, 19 percent Merlot, 14 percent Petit Verdot and 6 percent Cabernet Franc.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: Decanter's 2021 en primeur verdict (cool classicism, low alcohol) and The Wine Society (alcohol 1 to 2 percent lower); the 2021 blend from wine.com, Millesima and Berry Bros listings

facts.fact: Left out: whether the 2021 Gloria was the estate's first vintage in organic or biodynamic conversion (sources disagree); the vineyard area (48 to 50 hectares by source); scores.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026; not confirmed by two sources, or volatile

bottles.name: Château La Tour de Mons
bottles.card: Château La Tour de Mons Margaux 2020

facts.fact: Château La Tour de Mons is at Soussans, in the north of the Margaux appellation, named for Pierre de Mons, who came to own it in 1623; it is not an 1855 classed growth. Checked 28 November 2026 by the fact checker of chunk c4: one source has Pierre de Mons come to it by marriage to the daughter of the Baron de Soussans, another by purchase in 1623; the card’s came to own it holds either way. The producer record in research/winelist/producers-d.json says inherited, which no source found here supports.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: Wikipedia (Château La Tour de Mons); The Wine Cellar Insider; the Hachette producer page; Millesima's 2020 listing (Soussans). Sources differ on whether de Mons bought it or came to it by marriage (1615 or 1623), so the card says came to own it in 1623, as the producer record in research/winelist/producers-d.json gives it

facts.fact: The 2020 is 57 percent Merlot, 36 percent Cabernet Sauvignon, 4 percent Cabernet Franc and 3 percent Petit Verdot, aged in oak barrels, 25 percent new. Checked 28 November 2026 by the fact checker of chunk c4: Millesima gives 4 percent Cabernet Franc and 3 percent Petit Verdot; wine.com gives the 7 percent as Cabernet Franc alone. The card keeps Millesima’s figures, which the author found twice (English and French pages) and K&L repeats.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: Millesima (English and French pages) and K&L Wines for the blend; a retailer note and an importer's offer (Nick's) for 25 percent new oak (Flatiron gives 30 percent, the minority figure)

facts.fact: The 2020 tastes of plum, cassis and red berries with cedar and a rose petal perfume, with soft, ripe tannin. Checked 28 November 2026 by the fact checker of chunk c4: black cherry and lavender rest on one note (Michel Touton) and could not be found again, so the card no longer says them; brambly red fruit and pressed rose petal are the winemaker’s note on wine.com, plum and lilac James Molesworth’s, cassis and cedar The Wine Independent’s, velvety Cavissima’s, ripe tannin the Hachette guide’s.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: the winemaker's note on wine.com (brambly red fruit, pressed rose petal, potpourri); Michel Touton (black cherry, plum, lavender, sweet spice); The Wine Independent (cassis, cedar, bay leaf). No score is carried

facts.fact: 2020 in Bordeaux: a hot, dry summer and a small crop.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: Farr Vintners' 2020 overview (uniformly hot and dry summer); Jeroboams' 2020 report (long dry summer, hot dry harvest); a trade report of yields down by up to half

facts.fact: Left out: the vineyard area (35 to 58 hectares by source), the soils (one estate linked source only), the owners since 2019 or 2020 (sources disagree, and the owner named may be living).
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026; not confirmed by two sources, or a living person

bottles.name: Château Charmail Haut-Médoc • 1.5L Magnum
bottles.section: Large Formats > Red • Large Format > France

facts.fact: The list prints the magnum twice, the same bin, name, vintage and price: under Large Formats (b197, n 197, line 1052) and under France ~ Bordeaux ~ Red > Other Bordeaux (b2423, n 2423, line 12534). The card is filed under Large formats, as the October selection files every magnum printed under Large Formats.
facts.how: the catalogue research/winelist-2026-11-28.json and the paste; research/bottle-selection-2026-10-04.json (the Cos d'Estournel, Foillard and Duckhorn magnums)

facts.fact: It is the least expensive Bordeaux magnum the list prints: the next are the Cos Labory 2018 at $375 and the Château Clarke 2010 at $450. The work list's note that it is the only Bordeaux magnum under $600 does not hold.
facts.how: the catalogue research/winelist-2026-11-28.json, every 1.5L row of Bordeaux by price

facts.fact: Château Charmail is at Saint-Seurin-de-Cadourne, north of Saint-Estèphe near the Gironde, its vineyard one block beside Château Sociando-Mallet. Checked 28 November 2026 by the fact checker of chunk c4: The Wine Doctor has the two vineyards facing each other across the road a few hundred meters from Sociando-Mallet’s gate, which is how the producer record puts it, so the card says facing Sociando-Mallet across the road, not beside it.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: The Wine Cellar Insider (Charmail); The Wine Doctor; Lea & Sandeman's producer page; the producer record in research/winelist/producers-d.json. The area is given as 20 to 30 hectares by source, so the card gives none

facts.fact: Charmail is known for cold soaking (pre fermentation cold maceration) its red grapes, one of the first Left Bank estates to do so.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: The Wine Cellar Insider and The Wine Doctor; one source dates it to 1990, so the card gives no year

facts.fact: It is aged about twelve months in oak, about a third of it new, in recent vintages.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: Jancis Robinson (about one third new barriques each year); Lea & Sandeman (2018: twelve months, 30 percent new; 2023: 33 percent new); The Wine Cellar Insider (2016: twelve months, a third each new, one and two years old). The 2020 figures were not found; the card sends them to the sommelier

facts.fact: The 2020 is 36 percent Merlot, 32 percent Cabernet Sauvignon, 16 percent Cabernet Franc and 16 percent Petit Verdot. Checked 28 November 2026 by the fact checker of chunk c4: Millesima, Grand Cru Wijnen and Fareham Wine Cellar agree; Lea & Sandeman (41, 33, 15, 11) and Michel Touton (40, 33, 15) differ, so the 2020 sheet is the sommelier’s question if a guest asks.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: Jancis Robinson's tasting page and Millesima's listing

facts.fact: The 2020 tastes of dark plum and cassis, black fruit with a violet lift, with soft tannin. Checked 28 November 2026 by the fact checker of chunk c4: black cherry, dried herbs and licorice (given to Antonio Galloni) and pliant (to Neal Martin) could not be found in any search, so the card no longer says them; dark plums and cassis are James Suckling’s note, violet tinged black fruit Lea & Sandeman’s, soft tannins and red and black fruit Neal Martin’s as Lea & Sandeman quote it.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: Lea & Sandeman's note (floral, violet tinged black fruit); Vinous, Antonio Galloni (black cherry, gravel, dried herbs, licorice) and Neal Martin (pliant tannins). No score is carried

facts.fact: A magnum holds 1.5 litres, two bottles, about ten to twelve glasses; it ages more slowly, having about the same headspace and cork as a bottle for twice the wine.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: Wine Enthusiast (bottle size and aging) and Jancis Robinson (does bottle size matter); the Irish Times (about twelve glasses); the house's component Magnums and large formats

facts.fact: Left out: the Cru Bourgeois tier of the 2020 (sources give Supérieur and Exceptionnel), the owner (may be living), scores.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026

bottles.name: Jean Foillard "Côte du Py" Morgon Beaujolais • 1.5L Magnum
bottles.card: Jean Foillard ‘Côte du Py’ Morgon 2024 (1.5 L magnum)
bottles.section: Large Formats > Red • Large Format > France

facts.fact: The list prints the magnum twice, the same bin, vintage and price: under Large Formats (a231, n 227, line 1202) and under France ~ Burgundy ~ Red > Beaujolais (a2184, n 2162, line 11212). Both keys carry from the list of 3 October (n 231 and n 2184 there), so the 2024 magnum was printed then beside the 2023 magnum (bin 11371, $250), which the list of 28 November no longer prints. The card is filed under Large formats, as the October selection files every magnum printed under Large Formats.
facts.how: the catalogue research/winelist-2026-11-28.json, the ledger research/winelist/ledger.json and the October catalogue research/winelist-2026-10-03.json

facts.fact: The Côte du Py is the hill at the center of Morgon; its soil is decomposed schist (the roches pourries) over old volcanic rock, rich in iron and manganese.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: the importer's listing (Kermit Lynch, Côte du Py: schist, granite, manganese); a Morgon Côte du Py technical sheet of Mommessin (Boisset), weathered pyritic schist rich in iron oxide, roche pourrie as very old volcanic rock; Wine with Seth, Côte du Py climat and Morgon AOC pages. The standing components wine-region-beaujolais and cellar-foillard say the same. The hill's height (352 m, one sheet) is left out

facts.fact: The domaine farms vines from about ten to ninety years old and is certified organic.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: the importer's own product listing (Kermit Lynch: vineyard 10 to 90 years, 8.6 ha; farming organic, certified), a primary source. The hectares are left out

facts.fact: Made with whole bunches and native yeasts and bottled without fining or filtering.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: enbotella.com (grapes chilled before carbonic maceration, indigenous yeasts, bottled without fining or filtering) and primalwine.com (bottled without fining or filtration); whole bunches and native yeasts are in the standing components cellar-foillard and wine-story-gang-of-four. The barrel regime and its months could not be confirmed (one French retailer gives old Burgundy barrels, another source cement before bottling), so the card says nothing of them

facts.fact: 2024 in Beaujolais was a wet year with heavy mildew pressure and hail, and a small crop; the reds came out fresh.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: Decanter's French harvest 2024 reports (disease pressure and hail, significant losses in Beaujolais); Vitisphere, September 2024 (volumes down); M. Chapoutier's own 2024 Beaujolais harvest note (fresh and fruity reds); Wine Spectator (a late, low volume harvest; density and freshness). Vinous reports more green, underripe wines than usual in 2024, so the card says fresh and lively, never ripe or rich

facts.fact: The 2024 Côte du Py tastes of plum, red and black fruit, black tea and crushed stone, fresh and lively.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: the importer's note for the 2024 (Kermit Lynch: earthy stone and plum, serious minerality); Flatiron Wines' note for the 2024 (red and black fruit, black tea, crushed stone; fresh and lively on the entry). A white pepper finish given to one critic by one retailer is left out. No score is carried

facts.fact: A magnum holds 1.5 liters, two bottles, about ten to twelve glasses; wine ages more slowly in it, with about the same air under one cork for twice the wine. Gamay is served slightly cool, 55 to 58°F; a magnum takes longer to chill.
facts.how: the standing component wine-large-formats and the 2023 magnum card (overrides.json entries 1966 to 1971)

facts.fact: Left out: any named person. The label name is printed as the list prints it; the card speaks of the Foillard domaine and never of its living grower, and names none of the other living Morgon growers.
facts.how: the rule that nobody living is named in shipped text

bottles.name: Diebolt-Vallois "Blanc de Blancs" Extra Brut • 1.5L Magnum
bottles.card: Diebolt-Vallois ‘Blanc de Blancs’ Extra Brut NV (1.5 L magnum)

facts.fact: The list prints the magnum twice, the same bin, name and price: under Large Formats (a132, n 129, line 694) and under Champagne > Grower Producers ~ Côtes de Blancs (a401, n 398, line 2075). Both keys carry from the list of 3 October.
facts.how: the catalogue research/winelist-2026-11-28.json and the ledger research/winelist/ledger.json

facts.fact: It is the least expensive Champagne magnum the list prints: the next are Gamet Rive Gauche at $240 and Piper-Heidsieck Cuvée at $275 (the Luis Pato magnums at $190 and $200 are Portuguese sparkling wine, not Champagne). The next Blanc de Blancs magnum is Gaston Chiquet d'Aÿ 2014 at $420.
facts.how: the catalogue research/winelist-2026-11-28.json, every 1.5L row of Champagne by price

facts.fact: Diebolt-Vallois is a family grower in Cramant, a Grand Cru village of the Côte des Blancs.
facts.how: the standing producer record research/winelist/producers-c.json diebolt-vallois; search, 28 November 2026: Backroom Wines (eleven hectares in the chalky soils of Cramant), Gault&Millau's winery page, Premium Grands Crus' producer page. Cramant's Grand Cru rank is the échelle des crus, as the standing component wine-champagne-crus has it

facts.fact: The Blanc de Blancs is all Chardonnay, drawn from Cuis and Chouilly and neighboring villages; Cuis is a Premier Cru, so the blend does not carry the Grand Cru name.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: J.J. Buckley's note on the NV Extra Brut Blanc de Blancs (picked in Chouilly, Cuis and Épernay); Premium Grands Crus (Chouilly, Cuis and Épernay, with some young Cramant vines; Premier Cru Cuis and Grand Cru Chouilly); Tatler Asia's Champagne guide (Cramant, Chouilly, Cuis and Le Mesnil-sur-Oger, many of the grapes from Cuis). Only Cuis and Chouilly are in every source, so the card names those two and says neighboring villages for the rest

facts.fact: The bottling is Extra Brut: the appellation allows 0 to 6 grams of sugar a liter, and this one carries very little.
facts.how: the name the list prints; search, 28 November 2026: J.J. Buckley and Gault&Millau both name the NV Blanc de Blancs Extra Brut; Premium Grands Crus gives 3 g/l and three years on lattes. The dosage figure differs by source (2, 3, 3 to 5 g/l, some of them for the Prestige), so the card gives no number and sends it to the sommelier; the base vintages, which move with each disgorging, are left out

facts.fact: It tastes of lemon with a salty, iodine edge, taut and very dry.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: Gault&Millau's review of the Blanc de Blancs Extra Brut (lemony notes, a hint of saltiness, even iodine); J.J. Buckley (a salty nose); Jancis Robinson on the NV Blanc de Blancs (lemony). No brioche note was found for this cuvée, so the card gives none. No score is carried

facts.fact: Left out: the reserve wines kept in large casks in a chalk cellar and the perpetual reserve, which the sources tie to the house in general or to the Prestige, not to this bottling; and any family member's name (all living as far as can be told).
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: Premium Grands Crus, Flatiron Wines, the theis-vine.dk importer sheet (the Prestige)

bottles.name: Lucien Crochet Sancerre FR • 1.5L Magnum
bottles.card: Lucien Crochet Sancerre Rosé 2024 (1.5 L magnum)

facts.fact: The list prints the magnum twice, the same bin, vintage and price: under Large Formats > Rosé • Large Format (a196, n 192, line 1023) and under Rosé > France (a1442, n 1421, line 7379); the same rosé in 750 ml is printed beside it, the 2024 at bin 133422 (n 1420, line 7374) and the 2025 at bin 13434 (n 1422, line 7384), each $85. The Large Formats line prints no word rosé; its group heading does.
facts.how: the catalogue research/winelist-2026-11-28.json and the ledger research/winelist/ledger.json

facts.fact: It is the only still rosé the list prints in large format; the other rosé magnums are Champagne (Charles Heidsieck, Bollinger, Laurent-Perrier, Rare).
facts.how: the catalogue research/winelist-2026-11-28.json, every row larger than 750 ml whose name or heading says rosé

facts.fact: Lucien Crochet is a family estate in Bué, in the Sancerre appellation, growing Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir.
facts.how: the standing producer record research/winelist/producers-c.json lucien-crochet; search, 28 November 2026: Skurnik's producer page, The Wine Doctor, the importer Trialto's sheet (vineyards around Bué, Sancerre and Crézancy). The hectares differ by source (31, 35, 38) and are left out; the family members now running it are living and are not named

facts.fact: The rosé is all Pinot Noir, pressed straight away (direct pressing), and dry.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: wine.com's producer notes for the 2016 (direct pressed, whole berries into the press, temperature controlled tanks); 67wine.com and J.J. Buckley for the 2025 (100 percent Pinot Noir from Bué, direct pressed); Creamwine for the 2024 (100 percent Pinot Noir). Dry is the standing producer line. Hand harvesting, the Oxfordian and Kimmeridgian limestone, the months on lees and any oak (sources differ by vintage) are left out; the card sends the 2024 sheet to the sommelier

facts.fact: 2024 in Sancerre was a wet year with heavy mildew and a small crop; its wines are light, crisp and moderate in alcohol.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: the Centre-Loire wines body's 2024 harvest report (Sancerre yields 25 to 50 hl/ha, mildew pressure and rain at flowering); Vinous, Sancerre 2024 (mildew, tiny yields); Decanter, Centre-Loire 2024 (a light vintage, low alcohol, moderate concentration, very crisp acidity); Jancis Robinson's Loire vintage chart (low alcohol, high acidity). Frost is reported differently by source and is left out

facts.fact: The 2024 is crisp at the start, with melon and blood orange and an aniseed finish.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: the winemaker's notes for the Lucien Crochet Sancerre Rosé 2024 as wine.com prints them (crisp at the attack, melon, blood orange, an aniseed finish), the producer's own words. A note found for a 2024 Sancerre rosé of Dominique et Janine Crochet, another domaine, is not used. No score is carried

facts.fact: The list prints five Levet lines, all new on 28 November 2026: the 2022 bottle with no cuvée name (b2508, n 2508, bin 34331, line 12969, $240); the same 2022 in magnum (b2509, n 2509, bin 13231, line 12974, $490, and again under Large Formats as b228, n 228, line 1207); the 2023 (b2510, n 2510, bin 22711, line 12979, $250); Les Journaries 2022 (b2511, n 2511, bin 21562, line 12984, $260); Les Journaries 2022 in magnum (b2512, n 2512, bin 11271, line 12989, $540, and again under Large Formats as b229, n 229, line 1212). The card is the 2022 bottle at bin 34331.

facts.fact: Vignobles Levet is a small family estate in Ampuis whose vines are all Syrah, on both the Côte Brune and the Côte Blonde.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: Vente à la Propriété (Améthyste 2022 sheet: 100 percent Syrah, a blend of Côte Brune and Côte Blonde parcels); The Wine Cellar Insider (Bernard Levet profile: the vines are all Syrah, parcels on Côte Brune, Côte Blonde, Baleyat and Chavaroche); Shrine to the Vine; research/winelist/producers-d.json vignobles-levet (a small family estate in Ampuis)

facts.fact: The estate makes a house blend of all the family’s parcels, the step below Les Journaries and La Chavaroche; in the United States it is sold as plain Côte-Rôtie, as our list prints it, and European and some American retailers list it as Améthyste. The card calls it the house blend and does not print the name Améthyste, since no source ties bin 34331 to that label; the watch note sends any other cuvée name on the label to the sommelier.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: Wine Library (2022 Améthyste: the house cuvée, a selected blend from all the parcels the Levet family owns, quoting the importer); wine-wiki and Wine With Seth (Améthyste the entry Côte-Rôtie, Les Journaries the middle cuvée, La Chavaroche the top); wine.com and Westchester Wine list a 2022 Levet Côte-Rôtie with no cuvée name. That the bottle at bin 34331 is that house blend is inferred from the printed name and the price ($240 against $260 for Les Journaries)

facts.fact: The house blend is fermented with a large share of whole bunches and aged about two years in demi-muids and large casks, mostly old. The share of whole bunches is given variously (about half for the 2023, about 70 percent for the 2018, 60 to 70 percent in an importer note), so the card gives no figure and sends the 2022 figure to the sommelier.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: Madrose (importer notes: 30 to 40 percent destemmed for Améthyste and Journaries, 24 months in 600 liter demi-muids and 30 hectoliter foudres, 15 percent new); Farr Vintners (2018: 70 percent whole clusters, mostly neutral demi-muids); Comptoir des Millésimes (2023: about half whole clusters); iDealwine (two years in demi-muids); research/winelist/producers-d.json vignobles-levet (much of the stems, large casks and demi-muids)

facts.fact: Tasting words for the 2022 house blend: dark cherry and wild blackberry with spice, earthy and firm when young.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: Comptoir des Millésimes (2022 Améthyste: wild black berries, spices, dark cherries); Wine Library (2022 Améthyste: ripe red and black fruits, violets, smoked meats); research/winelist/producers-d.json vignobles-levet (dark, earthy, spiced and firm when young). Violet, smoked meat and rose petal rest on one retailer note and are left out. No score is carried

facts.fact: 2022 in the Northern Rhône was very hot and dry with a small crop; Côte-Rôtie came out structured and firm.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: Jancis Robinson (Northern Rhône 2022 vintage overview and chart: hottest and driest on record, very low yields); Decanter, Matt Walls (Northern Rhône 2022 report: yields down, Côte-Rôtie more structured than a typical year, tannic wines built to age). That Côte-Rôtie had more rain than the south of the Northern Rhône rests on one report and is left out

facts.fact: Côte-Rôtie: red wine from Syrah with up to 20 percent Viognier, which must be fermented together with it; most growers use little or none. The Côte Brune, on dark, iron-rich schist, gives firmer wine; the Côte Blonde gives more perfume. Ampuis is on the right bank near Vienne.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: the INAO cahier des charges of the AOC Côte-Rôtie (Syrah the principal variety, Viognier accessory, vinified together), Wikipedia (Côte-Rôtie AOC), Inter Rhône (vins-rhone.com), Decanter (Côte-Rôtie vignerons prefer Blondes; Brune and Blonde soils); the wine.com winemaker notes for the Levet 2022; the standing component cellar-rene-rostaing

facts.fact: Les Journaries comes largely from old vines in La Landonne and was first made in 2004; it is sold in Europe as Maestria.
facts.how: research/winelist/producers-d.json vignobles-levet (La Landonne, 2004); search, 28 November 2026: Wine With Seth and wine-wiki (Les Journaries called Maestria in Europe, La Chavaroche called La Péroline); Berry Bros (Cuvée Maestria listing)

facts.fact: Left out: the estate's vineyard area (3.5 to 5 hectares by source); the year the estate began (1936 in one profile only); the name of anyone who runs it, since the family members named in the sources are living; the importer; scores.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026; not confirmed by two sources, a living person, or volatile

facts.fact: The list prints three Peay Pinot Noirs, all 2023 at $180 and new on 28 November 2026: Pomarium (b2678, n 2678, bin 15181, line 13847), Savoy Vineyard Anderson Valley (b2679, n 2679, bin 145131, line 13852) and Scallop Shelf (b2680, n 2680, bin 16651, line 13857), all under United States ~ Pinot Noir > Sonoma Coast & County; and the Les Titans Syrah 2013 (key a3054, n 3048, bin 153221, line 15715, $120, United States ~ Other ~ Red > Syrah), carried from 3 October. The card is the Scallop Shelf.
facts.how: the catalogue research/winelist-2026-11-28.json, the ledger research/winelist/ledger.json and the paste, lines 13847 to 13861 and 15715

facts.fact: Peay Vineyards is a family estate near Annapolis on the far Sonoma Coast, about four miles from the Pacific.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: the winery's own site (peayvineyards.com: Scallop Shelf, a vineyard site four miles from the Pacific; the press page Scouting Annapolis); Wine Travel Guides (Peay Vineyards: 4 miles from the Pacific); research/winelist/producers-c.json peay (a family estate on the far Sonoma Coast). That it is one of the coolest sites in California stands in the producer record but was not confirmed by search, so the card does not say it

facts.fact: Scallop Shelf, Pomarium and Ama are the three estate Pinot Noir blends, each a combination of three to six clones and blocks chosen by barrel after the wine is made, not a single block. Scallop Shelf is named for the scallop and nautilus fossils found in the soil when the vineyard was prepared for planting; the winery describes it as floral and red fruited, graceful and elegant, and Pomarium as its muscle, with Ama between the two.
facts.how: the winery's own site, a primary source (peayvineyards.com/wines/pinot and the wine archives for Scallop Shelf and Ama), found by search 28 November 2026. One guide calls Scallop Shelf a single block from the oldest vines; the winery says otherwise and the card follows the winery

facts.fact: The Savoy Vineyard bottling is from bought fruit, the Savoy Vineyard in Anderson Valley, Mendocino County, more fruit forward and approachable young than the estate wines.
facts.how: the winery's own site (wine archives, 2016 Savoy: the site chosen outside the estate to hedge risk; more fruit forward and approachable in youth); Decanter and Wine Spectator listings of the 2023 Savoy as Anderson Valley, Mendocino County

facts.fact: The 2023 label reads West Sonoma Coast. The West Sonoma Coast appellation was approved by the TTB in 2022, lies entirely within the Sonoma Coast appellation and contains the Fort Ross-Seaview appellation.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: Wine Spectator, Jancis Robinson and the winery's members site list the 2023 Scallop Shelf as West Sonoma Coast; the Federal Register final rule of 23 May 2022 and the TTB; North Bay Business Journal and The Beverage Journal on the approval

facts.fact: 2023 on the Sonoma Coast: a wet winter and a cool spring delayed budbreak, the harvest came late, and the wines are fresh.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: James Suckling (In Sonoma's cool 2023, freshness comes to the fore); Bruliam Wines (heavy winter rain and a cool, wet spring, a late harvest); Senses Wines 2023 sheet (cool spring, late budbreak)

facts.fact: Tasting words for the 2023 Scallop Shelf: red and black cherry, jasmine tea and forest floor, floral and fresh.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026: the winery's members site (2023 Scallop Shelf: jasmine tea and forest floor under the fruit); Wine Spectator's 2023 note as quoted (mulled red and black cherry); Pogo's Wine (dark fruit, tea leaves); the winery's description of Scallop Shelf as floral and red fruited. Lavender, licorice and a saline note rest on one source each and are left out. No score is carried, and the members site's own superlative is not repeated

facts.fact: Left out: the 2023's oak regime, its fermentation and alcohol (not found), the clone shares (one retailer gives Pommard, 777 and 115 with no vintage), the year the estate was planted and its acreage (sources differ), the founders and the winemaker by name (living), and its price at the winery.
facts.how: search, 28 November 2026; not confirmed by two sources, a living person, or volatile
